subject: Puzzling behaviour in Shiny: t-statistics calculated twice and differently?!

messages.author: 3c613002e8f4925d
messages.subject: Puzzling behaviour in Shiny: t-statistics calculated twice and differently?!
parts:
Dear all,

I have a rather strange thing going on, and I cannot find the cause. Although it is not a real 'problem', I am intrigued to know 'why?'.

In short:
This Shiny app (for now) allows the user to draw increasing sample sizes from a normal distribution. It then plots a histogram for each given sample size and calculates the accompanying t-statistic.

The strange thing:
When you fire up the app (and keep the default settings), you will notice in the console (assuming you use RStudio) that when you press the 'Press me' button the second time, the t-statistic is calculated twice. And this keeps occuring when you continue to press the button. I would expect from my own scripts that it should only be calculated once?
Also, the two t-statistic values are always different, which makes me even more puzzled on how R/Shiny computes the first* value.

*I know for sure that the second value is the right one, as I checked it manually with the following code:

sample_size <- 2 # You can increase this number to manually 'simulate' the Shiny App's 'Press me' button
set.seed(123)
data <- rnorm(sample_size, 0, 1)
t_statistic <- (mean(data) - 0) / (sd(data) / sqrt(sample_size))
t_statistic # Check this value with the second t-statistic value after you pressed the 'Press me' button the second time

Here are the accompanying scripts:

#### Launch script ####

install.packages("shiny")

library(shiny)

setwd("") # Set working directory

runApp("", display.mode = "showcase") # Create a folder to store the app scripts


#### ui.R ####

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  
  # Title of Shiny app
  titlePanel("My World-dominating Shiny App"), 
  
  # sidebarLayout() embodies the widget and output panels
  sidebarLayout(
    
    # sidebarPanel() displays all widgets
    sidebarPanel(
      
      # Hypothesis test widgets
      sliderInput(inputId = "h0", 
                  label = "What should the null hypothesis mean value be?", 
                  min = -10, 
                  max = 10, 
                  value = 0), 
      
      # helpText() displays information in the app ui
      helpText("Set the desired value by which to increase the sample size 
               with each step. Then keep pressing the almighty 'Press me' 
               button to see some black magic."), 
      
      # Press the almighty button below to manually increase sample size by 1, 10 or 50 (depending on your choice)
      
      # Widgets to increase sample size manually and the size of the increase
      fluidRow(
        
        column(7, radioButtons(inputId = "step_size", 
                               label = "Sample size", 
                               choices = c("1", 
                                           "10", 
                                           "50"), 
                               inline = TRUE)
        ),
        
        column(5, actionButton(inputId = "step", 
                               label = "Press me")
        )
        
      )

    ), 
    
    # Output panel displaying the reactive outputs
    mainPanel(plotOutput("plot"),
              #tableOutput("table")
              textOutput("text"))
  )
))


#### server.R ####

shinyServer(function(input,output){
  
  ## Object values for server.R (in order of appearance)
  
  seed <- 123 # Setting the seed for set.seed()
  # number of samples drawn from rnorm()
  sample_size <- reactive({(input$step * as.integer(input$step_size))})
  # Reactive input by user, determining the mean of the drawn samples
  sample_mean <- reactive({input$h0})
  sample_sd <- 1 # Standard deviation of the drawn samples
  true_mean <- 0 # The true mean you want to test your H0 with
  
  
  ## Reactive outputs are returned to ui.R
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    
    # If/else statement for plotting histogram, text and t-statistic value
    
    if (sample_size() == 0){
      
      # If sample_size is 0, then an 'empty histogram' is plotted
      plot(NULL, 
           main = paste("Histogram of sampled data \nSample size:", sample_size()), 
           xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), 
           xlab = "Sample values", ylab = "Frequency", 
           bty = "n")
      
      # Text indicating that t-statistic cannot be computed
      output$text <- renderText({
        print("Need sample size > 1 to calculate t-statistic (1)")
      })
      
    }
    
    else { # If sample_size is not equal to 0, 
           # then a histogram of the sampled data is plotted
      
      set.seed(seed) # set.seed() to ensure replicable rnorm() data
      data <- rnorm(sample_size(), sample_mean(), sample_sd) # Sampling the data
      
      # Plot the histogram of the data
      hist(data, 
           main = paste("Histogram of sampled data \nSample size:", sample_size()), 
           xlab = "Sample values", ylab = "Frequency", 
           col = "gray")
      
      output$text <- renderText({
        
        # Text indicating that t-statistic cannot be computed
        if (sample_size() < 2){
          print("Need sample size > 1 to calculate t-statistic (2)")
        }
        
        # Calculate t-statistic and print its value
        else {

          data_mean <- mean(data) # Calculating the mean of the data
          data_sd <- sd(data) # Calculating the standard deviation of the data
          # Calculate t-statistic
          t_statistic <- (data_mean - true_mean) / (data_sd / sqrt(sample_size()))
          print(paste("t-statistic value =", t_statistic, "(3)"))
          
        }
        
      })
      
    }
    
  })
  
})

All help is much appreciated :)

Cheers
